conclusions: Model-only verification without evidence is useless: 1.4% (self) and 0% (cross-family) detection of fabrications.
A cross-family verifier abstains 52% of the time instead of detecting; family independence does not create knowledge.
With a reference, detection jumps to 99.65% but false alarms reach 72% on correct claims, because the model reads numeric formats loosely; a deterministic comparator is required.
Cost is not the obstacle (about 4 output tokens per item); validity is.
With an explicit numeric-tolerance instruction, false alarms fall from 72.2% to 44.4% but remain high: the failure is method-level (language comparison) not just formatting.
Cross-family verifier with the reference still fails: Mistral approved 177 answers while only 18 were correct, so providing evidence does not fix a verifier that does not compare.
